content.title: EuroBasket 2025 Fan Guide
content.text: FIBA EuroBasket 2025 features Europe's top 16 women's basketball teams competing for the continental title, with the top finisher earning an automatic qualification for the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup. The Golden State Valkyries will be well represented at the tournament, which takes place from June 18-29.Participating Valkyries*Janelle Salaün (France, Group A)Iliana Rupert* (France, Group A)Cecilia Zandalasini (Italy, Group B)Justė Jocytė* (Lithuania, Group B)Julie Vanloo (Belgium, Group C)Temi Fágbénlé (Great Britain, Group D)* Valkyries retain the rights to the player, who is not on the active 2025 roster at this timeScheduleFIBA EuroBasket Format16 TeamsEurope's top 16 Women's basketball teams compete for the continental title.4 GroupsThe 16 teams have been split into four groups and will play every team within their group once — the top two teams from each group advance to the quarterfinals.GroupsGROUP A: France*, Turkey, Greece, SwitzerlandGROUP B: Slovenia, Serbia, Italy*, Lithuania*GROUP C: Belgium*, Czech Republic, Montenegro, PortugalGROUP D: Great Britain*, Germany, Sweden, Spain* Valkyries RepresentationKnockout StageOnce the quarterfinals begin, it's win or go home until the championship game. The remaining eight teams will be seeded based their group play results.Championship GameOn June 29, the two semifinals winners will go head-to-head in the championship game, while the two semifinals losers will face each other in the third place game.When is FIBA EuroBasket 2025? Caret DownGroup Play: June 18-22 Knockout Stage: June 24-29Where Can I Watch? Caret DownWhat is at stake in FIBA EuroBasket 2025? Caret DownThe top three teams receive medals (Gold, Silver, Bronze) and the top five teams (besides host country Germany, who receives an automatic bid) secure a place in the 2026 FIBA Women's Basketball World Cup.Will the Valkyries roster change during FIBA EuroBasket 2025?
